Split strings

Source: R/replace.R
re_split.Rd

Splits each element of x at the matches of pattern, as Python's re.split() does: an empty match splits too, and with keep_groups = TRUE each separator's groups are kept between the pieces.

Usage

re_split(
  x,
  pattern,
  n = Inf,
  keep_groups = FALSE,
  flags = "",
  literal = FALSE,
  limits = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A character vector, a raw vector, or a list of raw vectors. NA (or NULL in a list) gives NA.

pattern

A character vector or an re vector; see Patterns.

n

The most pieces per element, Inf for no limit. The last piece holds the rest of the string, as with Go's Split(n); n = 0 gives no pieces.

keep_groups

If TRUE, the groups of each separator are inserted after the piece before it, NA for a group that did not take part.

flags

A single string of flag letters for pattern strings, such as "i" for case-insensitive matching; see re_compile() for every letter. It applies to every pattern in the call.

literal

If TRUE, each pattern string is matched as literal text, with no metacharacters, as base R's fixed = TRUE. Only the flags i and r apply to a literal pattern.

limits

A re_limits() object, or NULL for getOption("zuregex.limits") and then PCRE2's defaults.

Value

A list as long as x of character vectors; NA for an NA subject or pattern.

Patterns

pattern is a character vector of regular expressions, compiled through the cache with flags and literal, or an re vector from re_compile(), which carries its own flags and can use the JavaScript dialect. It has length 1, used for every element of x, or exactly the length of x, pairing pattern[i] with x[i]. Any other length is an error: nothing is recycled. An NA pattern gives NA for its element.

Base R's options map onto these arguments: ignore.case = TRUE is flags = "i", fixed = TRUE is literal = TRUE, invert = TRUE is re_detect(negate = TRUE), and useBytes = TRUE is a raw vector or strings marked as "bytes" (see Strings and bytes). perl = TRUE is always on.

Strings and bytes

Character input is matched as UTF-8; strings in other declared encodings are translated first. Invalid UTF-8 is an error of class zuregex_error_utf. A raw vector is one subject matched as bytes, as is each element of a list of raw vectors, and so is a character vector with any element marked as "bytes". Patterns are then compiled without UTF-8 support, so . matches one byte. \\C, which matches one byte, is allowed only then: in a UTF-8 pattern it is a compile error, since it could split a character.

Examples

re_split(c("a, b,c", "d"), ",\\s*")
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "a" "b" "c"
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] "d"
#> 
re_split("a1b22c", "(\\d+)", keep_groups = TRUE)
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "a"  "1"  "b"  "22" "c" 
#> 
re_split("a-b-c-d", "-", n = 2)
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "a"     "b-c-d"
#>
